items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Albert Hammond, maybe Leadbelly was on there

ctx.x: And then the next important part in the movie, I guess, they have us doing -- oh, after the band -- that's because the band leader in certain scenes where we're playing at the Palomar Ballroom in Los Angeles, I guess, and the success of the band, and all of a sudden, after flopping along the line, then the tremendous success. And then, of course, the movie ends with the Carnegie Hall Concert in 1938, with the tremendous triumph of the band, the first all jazz concert in Carnegie Hall.

But for the record, I think it should be made clear that that wasn't the first jazz in Carnegie Hall. Count Basie played in Carnegie Hall before Goodman, in a program called "Spiritual Swing." They had the Golden Gate Quartet on there and I think the boogie-woogie pianist, Pete Johnson, Albert Hammond, maybe Leadbelly was on there. And Basie represented the swing. Do you remember that concert?
